core_question.answer: The available source models do not justify treating Yellow and Red as mutually exclusive episode segments. UkraineAlarm has a real preserved snapshot where an older Yellow and newer Red coexist inside one AIR object. Alerts.in.ua models threats[] as the set of currently open threat components. Kyiv Digital models causes[] as a set where several causes may be active simultaneously.

verdict.title: RAW DIFFERENTIATED-ALERT TRANSITION PROOF

UkraineAlarm.direct_raw_proof_note: No direct authenticated upstream capture in this environment; real upstream /alerts dumps preserved by third-party repos were inspected and therefore remain SECONDARY_CONFIRMED.

Alerts.in.ua.direct_raw_proof_note: No direct authenticated upstream capture in this environment; a preserved active API response was inspected as SECONDARY_CONFIRMED evidence.

Kyiv official.direct_raw_proof_note: Current /state payload was directly captured (RAW_PROVEN); /history raw rows were not.

verdict.EPISODE_SEMANTICS: A Yellow-to-Red escalation does not safely imply a new AIR episode. The canonical parent must remain the continuous AIR period until all-clear, while differentiated threats are child state/components. UkraineAlarm proves Yellow and Red can coexist inside one active AIR object; Kyiv and Alerts.in.ua are also set-valued by schema.
verdict.NEXT_SCHEMA_CONSTRAINT: Use parent AIR episode + 0..N timestamped source threat/state observations/components. Preserve source IDs where they exist, region/type identity where they do not, raw level/cause/reason/timestamps, and do not force mutually exclusive level segments or infer component end times without transition evidence.
